target_evidence: The translated main target is the requested universally quantified backward-error theorem for the explicitly defined rounded dot product: S(Q)=D_M(T), with Q a componentwise gamma(depth(T)+1,u) perturbation of exactProductTree(T). Its recursive algorithm rounds each product once and each internal addition once. Conversely, the original target gives this same main claim; the auxiliary operation equations are definitions of the supplied constructions, and the auxiliary product bound follows directly from r(ab)=ab(1+delta) and |delta|<=u. These auxiliary statements impose no additional mathematical assumptions.

requirements.requirement: Prove the full universally quantified dot-product backward-error theorem.
requirements.evidence: dotProductBackwardError quantifies over every model M and every finite nonempty ordered binary tree T of real pairs. Under (depth(T)+1)u<1 it asserts an existential Q with both IsPerturbation(gamma(depth(T)+1,u),E(T),Q) and S(Q)=D_M(T), recovering the full requested backward-error conclusion.

requirements.requirement: Relate perturbations to exact componentwise products x_i*y_i.
requirements.evidence: E=exactProductTree maps each input leaf (a,b) to the exact real product ab and preserves ordered shape. The main target compares Q directly with E(T), explicitly giving |q-ab| <= gamma(depth(T)+1,u)|ab| for every corresponding leaf.

requirements.requirement: Account for one rounded multiplication per leaf.
requirements.evidence: The construction defines D_M(leaf((a,b)))=r(ab); roundedProductTerm and roundedProductTree identify precisely one rounded multiplication at every leaf. roundedProductTree_isPerturbation also establishes |r(ab)-ab| <= u|ab|. The main bound includes this multiplication error through the additional 1 in depth(T)+1.

requirements.requirement: Account for every rounded tree addition in the reduction.
requirements.evidence: The actual algorithm is D_M(node(L,R))=r(D_M(L)+D_M(R)), with the supplied tree preserved. Every internal-node addition is rounded, and the main target equates this very output with S(Q). Thus the asserted bound covers all ancestor additions, including in unbalanced trees.

requirements.requirement: Establish the gamma(depth+1,u) componentwise perturbation bound.
requirements.evidence: depth(leaf)=0 and depth(node(L,R))=1+max(depth(L),depth(R)). The main target uses gamma(depth(T)+1,u)=((depth(T)+1)u)/(1-(depth(T)+1)u) at every leaf. Each leaf has one product rounding and at most depth(T) ancestor additions; the stated smallness condition makes this denominator positive.

requirements.requirement: Use only the stated model and smallness assumptions without assuming or restricting the conclusion.
requirements.evidence: The model requires only real u>=0 and a rounding function satisfying for every real z the relative-error representation r(z)=z(1+delta) with |delta|<=u. The main theorem adds only (depth(T)+1)u<1. There is no exact-arithmetic restriction, balancing restriction, restriction on input values, or assumption of the perturbation conclusion.
